category_title: Struggling readers who use direct repetition of previous text to avoid new reading
minimal_context: The student and interventionist are taking turns reading 'Miss Nelson is missing!' together.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's continue reading 'Miss Nelson is missing!'. I will read this sentence: 'The class was rude.' Now it is your turn.

STUDENT: Was rude or that one.

TUTOR: I just read that part. Please look at the next line and read it.

STUDENT: (Accepts the speaking turn but does not attempt the unread text) Was rude.

TUTOR: (Points to the next passage of text) Go ahead and read this next one.

STUDENT: You 's gonna read the next one. I read this one.

options.A: Allow the student to select a book from several choices and use a constructivist approach to mediation, implementing scaffolds that focus on meaning and comprehension of the text.
options.B: Ask lower-level questions focused primarily on having the student recall additional factual information about the characters, setting, or plot of the selected book.
options.C: Continuously remind the student that they are expected to participate in the shared reading, even if they do not know the words or are not completely comfortable with the text.
options.D: Maintain a quiet and relaxing environment during the shared reading sessions, talking gently and slowly to the student while avoiding loud speech.
